Shiny bindings for grafts()

Source: R/shiny.R
grafts-shiny.Rd

Shows an explorer from grafts() in Shiny. The explorer tells the app what it shows, through inputs named after its output, and graftsProxy() lets the app steer it and replace its data.

Usage

graftsOutput(outputId, width = "100%", height = "600px")

renderGrafts(expr, env = parent.frame(), quoted = FALSE, lazy = NULL)

Arguments

outputId

Output variable to read from.

width, height

A CSS length for the explorer.

expr

An expression that returns an explorer from grafts().

env

The environment in which to evaluate expr.

quoted

Is expr a quoted expression (with quote())?

lazy

Serve each series through the session when it is drawn, rather than writing them all into the page. NULL (the default) serves data with more than 250,000 values.

Details

Small data are written into the page. Large data stay in R, which serves each series through the Shiny session when it is drawn, as the console and grafts_api() do. By default data with more than 250,000 values are served; set lazy to choose.

For an output "ts", the app can read these inputs:

  • input$ts_focus, the focused series, as a one-row data frame with a column for each key of the data, and NA for the keys it is aggregated over.

  • input$ts_children, the series of the focus's last split, one row each.

  • input$ts_pinned, the pinned series, one row each.

  • input$ts_split, the keys the children were split by, as a character vector.

  • input$ts_view, the view shown ("grid", "overlay", "stacked" or "season") and input$ts_set, the set it draws ("children" or "pinned").

  • input$ts_theme ("system", "light" or "dark") and input$ts_measure.

They are NULL until the explorer is drawn, and change as the visitor explores. Modules namespace them as for any output.

See also

graftsProxy() to steer the explorer and update its data.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
library(shiny)
tourism_agg <- fabletools::aggregate_key(
  tsibble::tourism, Purpose * (State / Region), Trips = sum(Trips)
)
ui <- fluidPage(graftsOutput("ts"), verbatimTextOutput("focus"))
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$ts <- renderGrafts(grafts(tourism_agg))
  output$focus <- renderPrint(input$ts_focus)
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
}
